summary: Interfaces is strategically pointed in the right direction and the codified priorities remain current, but health stays yellow because the assembly package is still not fully self-consistent or promotion-ready: assembly metadata contains broken documentation links, and downstream activation/verification evidence is still incomplete.

topPriorities.title: Resolve Interfaces identity, scope, and ownership boundaries
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Interfaces cannot function as a stable product if it collides with provider-owned interface artifacts or remains ambiguous about what it actually owns.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. Product, strategy, interfaces, risks, and decisions all reinforce the narrowed charter: cross-cutting standards, packaging, connectors, and change-governance discipline rather than ownership of every provider interface.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Keep the ownership stance explicit anywhere Interfaces is referenced, especially when boundary issues arise in downstream workspaces or other products.

topPriorities.title: Make the Interfaces assembly real, self-consistent, and consumable
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Verification and pinned-lane migration are not meaningful if the assembly package itself is path-broken or under-specified.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current and confirmed by evidence. The assembly exists, but assembly.yaml still points its changelog/activation/verify links at missing `assemblies/interfaces/v0.1/*` paths while the real files live under `assemblies/prompting-and-3pp/v0.1/*`.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Correct assembly metadata/documentation references and keep the packaged artifact set, install path, and verification surface internally consistent.

topPriorities.title: Run one downstream consumption pilot with evidence and one preventive drift guard
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Interfaces only becomes valuable when one real workflow proves the contracts improve execution quality and one preventive control reduces silent drift.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. Verify/activation expectations are stronger than before, but the evidence path is not yet closed: VERIFY still contains unchecked criteria and no linked workflow evidence is surfaced in the product stack reviewed here.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Require one real workflow evidence link in verification and enforce the changelog-plus-verification drift guard for meaningful interface-contract changes.

blockers.title: Assembly metadata/documentation path inconsistency
blockers.detail: assembly.yaml links to missing `assemblies/interfaces/v0.1/CHANGELOG.md`, `ACTIVATION.md`, and `VERIFY.md` paths, which weakens installability and auditability.

blockers.title: No closed-loop downstream verification evidence in reviewed stack
blockers.detail: The current verification artifact defines the required evidence but does not show a completed workflow evidence link or pass outcome in the reviewed materials.

risks.title: Identity and ownership collision
risks.detail: Interfaces could still drift back into a residual bucket or collide with provider-owned interfaces if the narrowed charter is not maintained.

risks.title: Assembly packaging remains not fully self-consistent
risks.detail: Broken or inconsistent assembly links reduce credibility of the package as a real export surface and undermine pinned-lane migration readiness.

risks.title: Promotion gate remains too thin
risks.detail: Without one real downstream workflow and linked verification evidence, the product cannot demonstrate behavioral value or control drift credibly.

proposedTdeActions.title: Treat Interfaces assembly self-consistency as the immediate overnight focus
proposedTdeActions.why: Priority 2 is validated by direct evidence of broken links in the current assembly surface.

proposedTdeActions.title: Require a real downstream verification evidence path before promotion claims
proposedTdeActions.why: Priority 3 remains open and directly tied to product value and drift prevention.

proposedTdeActions.title: Keep Interfaces charter bounded to standards/packaging/connectors
proposedTdeActions.why: Priority 1 remains the strategic guardrail preventing scope creep and ownership confusion.

priorityRefreshNotes: Reviewed PRODUCT.md, MODEL.yaml, VISION, STRATEGY, OPERATING_MODEL, PLAN, RISKS, METRICS, INTERFACES, DECISIONS, current TOP_PRIORITIES, and referenced assembly artifacts. TOP_PRIORITIES.md remains aligned with the stack; no refresh update was required in this run.
